Amsterdam → Lauterbrunnen → Kandersteg → Amsterdam

Three days of altitude, one of them spent falling

Five days, three people, one car. A via ferrata down a cliff, two nights above 2,000 metres, a paraglider back to the car park, and a lake to finish. Everything below is bookable, priced and mapped.

Day oneMonday 14 September

Drive south

Nine and a half hours if the Ruhr behaves. Buy the Swiss e-vignette before you cross, fill up in Germany, and aim to be eating in Stechelberg by eight.

Tap a photo to enlarge · more photos on Google

  1. 08:00

    Leave Amsterdam Zuidoost

    Utrecht, Cologne, Karlsruhe, Basel, Bern, Interlaken. Two stops, roughly 890 km.

    Fuel share CHF 36 · e-vignette CHF 40 per car
  2. 10:30

    Fill up past Emmerich

    German diesel and petrol are the cheap stretch. Use an Autohof just off the exit, not a motorway Rasthof, and save 15 to 20 cents a litre.

  3. 16:00

    Second fill near Karlsruhe

    Last cheap fuel before Basel. Top up here so you don't buy Swiss petrol.

  4. 18:30

    Park in Stechelberg

    Mürren and Gimmelwald are car-free, so the car lives here until Thursday, at the Schilthornbahn valley station. No booking, 24/7, cash or card at the machine. You cannot leave and re-enter without starting a new ticket.

    Barrier car park, ticket on entry, pay before you leave · ~CHF 25 for the three days
  5. 19:30

    Dinner and bed

    Valley kitchens stop around 20:30. If the drive runs long, Hotel Stechelberg serves on site and saves the search.

Day twoTuesday 15 September

Down the wall, then a long way up

The via ferrata runs one way from Mürren to Gimmelwald and there is no exit halfway, so it decides the shape of the morning. Afterwards you climb back out of the valley, keep climbing, and don't come down again until Thursday, by air. This is the biggest single day of the trip.

Tap a photo to enlarge · more photos on Google

  1. 08:00

    Cable car to Mürren

    Collect harness, ferrata set and helmet from Intersport in the village. Walk in, no booking needed.

    Lift ~CHF 11 · gear rental ~CHF 35
  2. 09:00

    Via ferrata to Gimmelwald

    2.2 km, 300 m of descent, about three hours, graded K3. Open 1 June to 31 October, 09:00 to 18:00. It closes in rain or with rain in the forecast.

    Route is free · guided from CHF 179 if anyone wants a pro
  3. 12:30

    Lunch in Gimmelwald

    Mountain Hostel does pizza and beer with a view. Eat properly, the afternoon is uphill.

    ~CHF 25
  4. 13:30

    Cable car back up to Mürren

    Five minutes, about CHF 7. Take it. The Sprutz waterfall path is lovely but the afternoon needs your legs.

  5. 14:00

    Mürren to Schilthornhütte

    2h15 and 800 metres up the Kanonenrohr path past Schiltgrat. Steady, relentless, no water on the way. Fill up in the village.

  6. 16:30

    Schilthornhütte, 2,433 m

    Twenty-five places in an upstairs dormitory, sun terrace, and showers in the basement, which is rare at this height and very welcome after a ferrata. Bring a sleeping bag or hire one there.

    ~CHF 90 half board · cancel 2 days ahead by 18:00 or CHF 50 pp

If it rains

The ferrata is closed. Go up to Mürren anyway, take the cable car to Birg and walk the 40 minutes down to the hut, then try to move the ferrata to Thursday morning in place of the flight. Both cannot slip to the same day, so decide at breakfast which one you want more.

Day threeWednesday 16 September

Summit before nine

You sleep high, so the summit is only an hour and a half away and you get it in the morning light, before the first gondola crowd and before the afternoon cloud builds. Then a long descent to a meadow hut, and an afternoon with nothing to do but climb a small green knoll and watch the light move across the Jungfrau.

Tap a photo to enlarge · more photos on Google

  1. 07:00

    Breakfast at the hut

    No rush, but the earlier you are on top the better the light and the emptier the terrace.

  2. 07:40

    Up to Birg

    Forty minutes out of the Engetal to the halfway station, 2,677 m.

  3. 08:30

    Ridge path to the summit

    About an hour along the crest from Birg. Leave the packs at the hut if you are coming back this way, and it becomes a stroll.

  4. 09:15

    Schilthorn, 2,970 m

    Piz Gloria at the top, revolving restaurant and all. Breakfast number two with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau in a row in front of you, before the first gondola crowd arrives.

    Coffee and cake ~CHF 20
  5. 10:30

    Down the Wasenegg ridge

    Two to two and a half hours, steep, with exposed sections. Descending this is harder than climbing it, so take it slowly and skip it entirely if the rock is wet.

    T3+ · see the gentle version below
  6. 13:00

    Rotstockhütte, 2,039 m

    A ski club hut in a meadow under the Schilthorn. You arrive early, which is the point. No showers. Dinner at a fixed time at shared tables.

    CHF 79 half board · cash only, francs or euros
  7. 16:00

    Bryndli, 2,133 m

    Optional, and the best forty minutes of the day. A grassy knoll just above the hut with the whole Lauterbrunnen valley below and the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau lined up opposite. Go with an empty pack, stay for the light, be back for dinner.

    40 min up, 25 down · easy trail

The gentle version

Descending the Wasenegg is the one properly exposed stretch of the trip. If it is wet, foggy or anyone is uneasy, go back to Birg from the summit and drop down the normal path past Grauseeli to Schiltalp, then across to Rotstockhütte. Adds about forty minutes, all on ordinary trail. You still get the ridge as an out-and-back from Birg with light packs, which is the nicer way to walk it anyway.

Day fourThursday 17 September

Fly down, drive west, walk to a lake

The only day with a hard deadline. You descend to Mürren, fly to within fifty metres of the car, and are in Kandersteg by lunch. The afternoon is the turquoise one.

Tap a photo to enlarge · more photos on Google

  1. 06:45

    Breakfast, then the North Face Trail

    Two hours of easy descent to Mürren via Schiltalp, with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau in front of you the whole way. Leave by 07:00 to keep slack before the flight.

  2. 09:00

    Meet Airtime in Mürren

    Ten minutes uphill on foot to the take-off field, a briefing, a few running steps, and The Wall: 12 to 20 minutes above the Lauterbrunnen valley.

    CHF 199 · photos and video extra, paid to the pilot after
  3. 10:00

    Land in Stechelberg

    The landing field is beside the Schilthornbahn station. The car is right there. Pay the parking, load up.

  4. 11:00

    Drive to Kandersteg

    68 km via Interlaken, Spiez and Frutigen. About an hour and fifteen. Park at the hotel and go up empty-handed.

  5. 12:30

    Gondola to Oeschinen

    A time slot must be reserved online in addition to the ticket, from 20 June to 20 September. Book it before you leave home.

    ~CHF 22 one way
  6. 13:15

    Underbärgli and Oberbärgli loop

    About three hours above the north shore, with real climbing in it and the best angle on the Blüemlisalp wall. Lunch at the lakeside restaurant first.

  7. 16:30

    Walk down to Kandersteg

    1h15 on the trail from the lake, coming out at the cable car valley station. Then about half an hour across the village to the hotel, or take the local bus.

  8. 18:30

    Pool, sauna, dinner

    After two hut nights, the Doldenhorn spa is the entire argument. Pool open until 22:00, and guests can use it before check-in and after check-out.

No wild camping at Oeschinensee

Tents, bivouacs, hammocks and sleeping outdoors are banned by court order across the whole area, rangers patrol it, and the fine runs to CHF 2,000. The hotel is the plan.

Two things to confirm when booking the flight

First, what is actually bookable before 09:30, since September mornings here get valley fog. Second, whether the pilot can take a small daypack, because you will be coming straight off the hut descent with everything you own. Keep packs to about 30 litres for the whole trip.

Airtime advise booking early in a trip so there is room to reschedule for weather. Yours is on the last morning, so hold Wednesday midday as an informal backup: you pass through Mürren anyway.

North

Breakfast, spa if there is time, then 890 km home. Leave by eight and you are back for a late dinner.

    Included. The spa is also open before check-out at noon if anyone wants one more soak.

    Frutigen, Spiez, Bern, Basel, Karlsruhe, Cologne, Utrecht. About nine and a half hours.

What it costs

Per person, three of you sharing one car and twin or triple rooms. Swiss francs. Hut prices are confirmed, hotel prices are estimates until you call.

  • Bring about CHF 250 each in cash. Both huts are cash only, in francs or euros, and neither takes cards reliably.
  • Swap Doldenhorn for Ermitage and Thursday drops by roughly 50 each, total about 730 without the flight.
  • The single-room supplement is the wildcard. Three people means a double plus a single unless the hotel has a triple, and singles carry a CHF 50 to 75 surcharge. Ask.
  • Not included: the Schilthorn cable car if you use it as a bail-out, photos from the pilot at CHF 40, and drinks beyond the 15 a night budgeted at the huts.

Kit that the trip actually requires

  • Sleeping bag liner. Mandatory at both huts. Rentals cost 5 to 9 a night, so bring one.
  • One 30-litre pack each. You carry everything over the ferrata, up the ridge, and possibly into the tandem harness. Huts supply bedding.
  • Insulated layer, gloves, hat. Nights at 2,433 m in mid-September sit near freezing.
  • Headtorch. Dark by 20:00, and the hut basements are not brightly lit.
  • Waterproof shell. No rain gear, no ferrata, and the Wasenegg ridge in wet rock is a different proposition.
  • Cash in francs. Say it three times, it still catches people out.
  • Indoor shoes. Boots come off at the hut door.
